name: Authentication & Authorization Patterns
description: Enforces secure authentication and authorization best practices including JWT handling, session management, and RBAC.
content:
# Authentication & Authorization Patterns Rules

- Use established auth libraries (Passport.js, NextAuth, Supabase Auth, Firebase Auth) — never build auth from scratch
- Hash passwords with bcrypt, scrypt, or Argon2id — never use MD5, SHA-1, or unsalted hashes
- Store JWT tokens in HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookies — never in localStorage or sessionStorage
- Set short JWT expiration (15 minutes for access tokens) with longer-lived refresh tokens stored server-side
- Implement refresh token rotation — issue a new refresh token on each use and invalidate the old one
- Use RBAC (Role-Based Access Control) or ABAC (Attribute-Based Access Control) — check permissions on every protected endpoint
- Apply authorization checks at the API layer, not just the UI — hiding a button is not access control
- Implement account lockout after 5-10 failed login attempts — with exponential backoff or CAPTCHA
- Require MFA for admin accounts and sensitive operations — TOTP, WebAuthn, or SMS as fallback
- Use CSRF tokens for cookie-based auth — not needed for Bearer token auth
- Log all authentication events — successful logins, failed attempts, password resets, permission changes
- Implement session invalidation on password change — force re-authentication across all devices
